optimization: Build snapshot rows in place in already-reserved vector storage (ExportDirectorySnapshotBounded's child loop, and ParseSnapshot's entry loop) instead of on the stack and then moving them in.
target: First-generation delivery (export row and client parse row)
method: Interleaved randomized idle-gated A/B in one session, 6 processes per arm, 5 warm-up + 5 measured repetitions, release-test preset.
noise_spread: Decisive evidence that the effect is below the noise floor: the SAME baseline binary was re-measured in two different idle-gated sessions and produced TOTAL median-of-run-medians of 91.799 ms and 96.992 ms -- a 5.7% difference with no code change whatsoever. The candidate's apparent -4.31% is inside that baseline-only run-to-run variation. Export moved -0.08% (no signal at all) while publish moved +3.5% against the change's intent.
correctness_checks: ffprotocol_tests passed with zero failures and the full release-test CTest suite passed 124/124 with the change in place. No semantic change: identical field values, identical reject-whole-batch discipline.
reason: The targeted rows did not improve: export -0.08% and publish +3.5%. The one favorable row (TOTAL -4.31%) cannot be attributed to the change because the unchanged baseline binary alone varies by 5.7% between sessions on this host. Retaining a change whose measured effect is indistinguishable from a no-op run of the same binary is exactly what section 13 forbids, so it was reverted.
note: Both call sites already reserve exact capacity, so the reserved storage was present on both sides and only the redundant 112-byte row move was removed. That move was evidently cheap relative to the real dominant cost identified by profiling: per-entry std::wstring heap allocation in the 200,000-row projection-to-snapshot conversion.
